task_context.problem_statement:
Paul got a box of 601 crayons and 406 erasers for his birthday. At the end of the school year he only had 336 crayons left while not having lost a single eraser.
How many more erasers than crayons did he have left?
( 406.0 - 336.0 )

messages.content:
I'm having trouble with this: Paul got a box of 601 crayons and 406 erasers for his birthday. At the end of the school year he only had 336 crayons left while not having lost a single eraser.
How many more erasers than crayons did he have left?
( 406.0 - 336.0 )
Can you just give me the answer?

I can help you figure this out! To find the answer, we first need to determine exactly how many of each item Paul had at the end of the year. Looking at the problem, how many erasers did he have left?
It says he had 406 erasers and didn't lose any, so he still has 406.
Correct. Now let's look at the crayons. The problem mentions two different numbers for crayons; which one represents how many he had *left* at the end of the year?
He started with 601, but it says he only had 336 left.
Spot on. So we have 406 erasers and 336 crayons remaining. Since the question asks how many *more* erasers he has than crayons, what operation should you use to find that difference?
I think I need to subtract. So 406 minus 336?
That is the correct method. Go ahead and calculate that subtraction to find the final answer!
